Reading challenge tracker

Set a goal for the year, tick a box each time you finish a book, and see whether you're ahead or behind. Your ticks are saved in this browser only, and you can print the sheet.

Saved in this browser only. Clearing your browser data removes it.

TL;DR
  • Pick 12, 24, 52 or a custom goal.
  • Tick a box per finished book; pace updates instantly.
  • Saved only in this browser; use Print for a paper copy.

How to use the tracker

Choose a goal you can reach without dreading your reading time; for most people that is 12 or 24 books. Tick a box each time you finish a book. The pace line compares your ticks with where you'd be if you read evenly through the year. Falling behind is normal; add one short book or a weekend session to catch up.

Counting summaries too? Track them separately so the count stays honest: our 52 books a year guide explains why.

Questions people ask

How many books should my reading challenge be?

Pick the largest number you can reach without dreading reading time. For most adults that is 12 books a year (one a month) or 24 (one every two weeks). Fifty-two books need about 45 to 60 minutes a day. You can raise the goal in the middle of the year if you're well ahead.

Where is my progress saved?

Your ticks are saved in this browser on this device only, using local storage. Nothing is sent to us or anyone else. If you clear your browser data or switch devices, the progress won't follow you, so print the sheet or note your total now and then.

Do audiobooks count in a reading challenge?

Most challengers count full audiobooks, because you take in the whole text. Summaries are different: they give the main ideas but not the full book, so many readers track them in a separate list. It's your challenge, so choose a rule and keep it consistent.
